$comment: OBS3 — Langfuse score configs for AgentB2C, versioned in git so they're re-creatable on any instance (score configs are project-scoped, no bulk-import API — this file is the source of truth, POST /api/public/score-configs per entry to restore). Mirrors the 16 configs actually created on the project's Langfuse instance on 2026-07-30 (project cms4gd0d20002nz029tuly62e). The contract for the `guard_*` names is GUARD_SCORE_NAMES in libs/b2c_common/b2c_common/scores.py — never rename an entry once it has real data.

known_gaps.name: guard_date_hallucinated_year_rolled_forward
known_gaps.reason: 43 chars — exceeds Langfuse's score config name limit (createScoreConfig: maxLength 35). No config exists for this guard; the score itself (b2c_common.scores.score_guards) still emits fine without one — config_id is optional, it only adds UI-side min/max/category validation. Not yet wired for emission either way (hotel_search_agent is out of OBS3's zone).

known_gaps.name: degraded
known_gaps.reason: CATEGORICAL score config creation via the langfuse MCP server's createScoreConfig tool rejected every categoricalCategories payload tried (array of {label, value} objects, string values, numeric values, even a 2-entry throwaway test) with the same generic 'Category must be an array of objects with label value pairs, where labels and values are unique' error — looks like a bug in that MCP tool's request serialization, not a payload issue. No config exists for `degraded`; b2c_common.scores.score_degraded emits it fine without one (config_id optional, closed set enforced in code already). Retry creating this one config via the Langfuse UI directly (Project Settings -> Scores) next time someone is in there — trivial once the tool bug is understood or the UI is used instead of the MCP tool.
